items.title: Sands interviewed by Monk Rowe, 2019
items.q: [INTERVIEWER] I had an interesting experience mid-week I happened to catch a Nat King Cole documentary... And the next day I found you playing “L-O-V-E” on a video for WGBO.

ctx.x: Because well it affects not only the song list but how you play, how you present the music. Because you know you want to have fun in the space that you’re in you know, so if you have a dry space you might play tunes that kind of fit that mold or fit that type of — you know it’s brightly lit so you want to do bright songs, or something like — or something to darken the mood. You know you’ve kind of got to figure out how to play with the environment that you’re in, you know. Yeah.

I had an interesting experience mid-week I happened to catch a Nat King Cole documentary. And near the end they talked about the song “L-O-V-E” which was a hit for him. And the next day I found you playing “L-O-V-E” on a video for WGBO. Do you remember it?
I do. I do remember it.
